content.new_article_detail: 2,427 words, full Article + BreadcrumbList + BlogPosting + FAQPage, 23 internal links, 0.56s TTFB, present in sitemap and already server-rendered into the /articles listing without manual intervention.
content.shared_chrome_change: The 07 Aug footer/nav trim has held steady for three days (core 17 links, projects 17, articles 20-24; per-page word counts within about +/-10 of 07 Aug). No second drop and no recovery, so it reads as a deliberate one-off change rather than a regression. /articles is at 71 links, up exactly one for the new article.

notes: Health holds at 88 (raw 87.7 -> 88.3). Performance 92 -> 94 and Content 79 -> 80; Crawlability, Structured Data and On-page are unchanged because no fix was deployed since 07 Aug. Two open items: P1 JSON-LD duplication (day 8) and P2 homepage/project alt text plus lazy-loading (day 11). The 07 Aug /articles listing fix is holding and absorbed the new article automatically.

onpage.note: Identical to 07 Aug on every image metric. Eleven days since the 30 Jul recommendation; the team did deploy today (new article + speed change), so the gap is queueing rather than release capacity.

performance.measurement_method: sequential (concurrency 1) same-origin fetch via Chrome; best of two sequential passes per URL to suppress network jitter, AbortController 15s
performance.note: All three groups improved vs 07 Aug: core 864 -> 714 ms, articles 775 -> 678 ms, projects 669 -> 573 ms. /interiors fell 1529 -> 855 ms, /modules 1164 -> 881, /model 1002 -> 864; a synchronised move across image-heavy core pages suggests a serving-layer or cache change rather than jitter alone. /studio moved the other way, 1035 -> 1352.

source: Chrome live crawl (same-origin fetch), no third-party SEO tool
